deliverables.title: ValidationRule Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won
deliverables.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<ValidationRule xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <fullName>Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won</fullName>
    <active>true</active>
    <description>Locks Opportunity Amount once Closed Won so the recorded deal value cannot be lowered after close. Owner: Sales Ops. Bypass: Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock (Sales Ops only).</description>
    <errorConditionFormula>AND(
  NOT($Permission.Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock),
  NOT(ISNEW()),
  ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"),
  Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)
)</errorConditionFormula>
    <errorDisplayField>Amount</errorDisplayField>
    <errorMessage>Amount cannot be decreased once this Opportunity is Closed Won. Amount is locked after close to protect the recorded deal value. Contact your manager to reopen the Opportunity before changing Amount.</errorMessage>
</ValidationRule>

deliverables.content:
# Deploy order — M1-S01 (Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won)

Build: `opp-amount-lock` · Step: `M1-S01` · Manifest: `package.xml` (`<version>67.0</version>`)

## The three components

| # | Type | Member | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CustomPermission` | `Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock` | `customPermissions/Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock.customPermission-meta.xml` |
| 2 | `PermissionSet` | `Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass` | `permissionsets/Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass.permissionset-meta.xml` |
| 3 | `ValidationRule` | `Opportunity.Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won` | `objects/Opportunity/validationRules/Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won.validationRule-meta.xml` |

## Ordering constraints

1. **`CustomPermission` before `PermissionSet`.** The permission set carries a *grant*, not the
   definition: `PermissionSet` and `Profile` "do not carry the permission's definition — only a grant
   of a permission that must already exist", and "A `PermissionSet` naming a custom permission that
   does not yet exist fails the deploy"
   (`skills/admin/custom-permissions/references/metadata-examples.md`, "Where the files live" and
   "Retrieve and deploy").

2. **`CustomPermission` before `ValidationRule`.** The rule's formula reads
   `$Permission.Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock`. The same reference section states the rule: deploy
   definitions "before any consumer that references them". The consumer here is the validation rule's
   `errorConditionFormula`.

3. **`PermissionSet` and `ValidationRule` are siblings** — neither references the other, so their
   relative order does not matter once (1) and (2) hold.

4. **One request is the safe shape.** All three members are in this step's `package.xml`, so a single
   `sf project deploy` request resolves 1–3 internally. Splitting the deploy is only necessary if the
   org already holds part of the set. `skills/devops/metadata-api-retrieve-deploy/references/gotchas.md`
   (L124) names `PermissionSet` ↔ `CustomPermission` ↔ custom-field cycles as a known
   "validation passes / deploy fails" hazard when cross-type references are split across requests —
   another reason to keep these three together.

5. **Dependency-driven sequence, if this step is folded into a larger release.**
   `skills/admin/change-management-and-deployment/references/llm-anti-patterns.md` (Anti-Pattern 4)
   orders a release: data model → code → flows → layouts/record types → **permission sets and
   profiles** → sharing rules → reports. This step contributes only to the "permission sets" band plus
   the object-embedded validation rule, so it deploys after any field or record-type change in the same
   release and before nothing.

## Dependencies on components outside this step

**None.** Both fields the formula touches — `Amount` (Currency) and `StageName` (Picklist) — are
standard Opportunity fields already present in every target org; no step in this build creates them.
The rule is not scoped to a record type, so no `RecordType` is a prerequisite. `depends_on` for
`M1-S01` is empty in `plan.json`, and this note confirms that is correct rather than an omission.

## Post-deploy, not part of the deploy

- Assign `Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass` to the **two named Sales Ops users** (clarification Q3). The
  permission set deploys empty of assignees; an unassigned bypass is a bypass nobody holds.
- Assumption **A1** (`PLAN.md`): `Amount` is on the Opportunity page layout(s) in scope. If it is not,
  `errorDisplayField` "changes automatically to Top of Page"
  (`skills/admin/validation-rules/references/metadata-examples.md`, element table) and the error
  silently relocates. Confirm on the layout after deploy.
- Decision **D2** (`PLAN.md`): the rule deploys `active=true` against data that already contains a
  handful of lowered Closed Won Amounts. The delta check (`Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)`) means those
  records are not re-blocked on unrelated edits, but they stay non-conforming by design.

## Validate-only command — the human runs this, no agent does

```bash
sf project deploy validate \
  --manifest .sfskills/builds/opp-amount-lock/artefacts/M1-S01/package.xml \
  --source-dir .sfskills/builds/opp-amount-lock/artefacts/M1-S01 \
  --target-org <alias>
```

`sf project deploy validate` is documented for a **production** target and requires Apex tests; against
a sandbox use `sf project deploy start --dry-run` instead
(`agents/_shared/AGENT_CONTRACT.md`, Gate C). A validate-only deploy proves the XML parses and the
formula compiles. It does **not** prove the bypass works — that needs the two Apex tests in
`skills/admin/validation-rules/references/metadata-examples.md` ("Apex tests", Test 1 and Test 2), or
the manual acceptance line on milestone `M1`.

Nothing in this build deploys. This file is text for a human to copy.

formula_divergence.what_changed: The NOT(ISBLANK(StageName)) blank guard was dropped. Clause order and every other clause are unchanged.
formula_divergence.why: The invoking instruction specified this four-clause, bypass-first formula. It also resolves verification warning W4, which records that admin/validation-rules contradicts itself on ISBLANK over a picklist and offers NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(StageName))) as the reconciliation if the platform rejects a raw picklist argument.
formula_divergence.syntax_note: The invoking instruction wrote the clauses joined with `&&` and the literal as 'Closed Won' in single quotes. Both were rendered instead as AND(...) with double quotes: AND(...) is the canonical shape in templates/admin/validation-rule-patterns.md ('The canonical VR shape') and in every example in admin/validation-rules; single-quoted literals appear in this skill only inside references/llm-anti-patterns.md as an LLM anti-pattern, and Salesforce formula text literals take double quotes. The clause set and their order are exactly as instructed.
formula_divergence.cost: check_validation_rules.py line 418 raises a REVIEW finding when a formula contains ISPICKVAL( and no ISBLANK(. REVIEW carries severity weight 0 and is not in BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, so the checker still exits 0 and the acceptance test's `expected: exit 0` still holds.
formula_divergence.contradicted_guidance: skills/admin/validation-rules/SKILL.md '## Formula Best Practices' opens with 'Always guard picklist checks against blank' and gives the exact counter-example AND(NOT(ISBLANK(StageName)), ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won")). Its '## Proactive Triggers' table repeats it. This artefact does not carry that guard.
formula_divergence.why_it_is_nonetheless_safe_here: ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won") returns FALSE when StageName is blank, so the positive form cannot misfire on a blank picklist; the skill's warning is aimed at the NOT(ISPICKVAL(...)) form. StageName is a required standard picklist on Opportunity and cannot be blank on a saved record in any case.
remedies_for_the_human: Restore the guard in the W4-reconciled form NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(StageName))) — valid on a picklist, silences the REVIEW finding, and restores the plan's clause count.
Restore the plan's literal NOT(ISBLANK(StageName)) — matches plan.json exactly but is the form W4 flags as possibly not compilable against a raw picklist.
formula_divergence.plan_is_now_out_of_sync: plan.json.steps[].inputs.errorConditionFormula still carries the five-clause form. Reconciling it is `build_plan.py amend-step`, which neither this agent nor build-step-runner is authorised to run.
